doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Focal Point and Inner Voices with Bill Fischer
summary: Brown discusses the expanded front line on Focal Point and the horns-and-voices Inner Voices, conducted by Bill Fischer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So on this album Focal Point you have an expanded front line. You have Gary Bartz, and Joe Ford on reeds, and also Ron Bridgewater, I guess he is related to Cecil and Dee Dee.

And then Charles Fambrough on bass, so you keep expanding, now you’ve got a broadened front line coming out of this. And then when we get to Inner Voices, now this one also is a departure so, composed and arranged by McCoy Tyner plus horns and voices, so what was the inspiration for this project?
Is there a lot of voices on there? Inner Voices. Yeah I guess that’s why I named it like that.
It was good working with him, he knew how to deal with different types of ensembles, vocal things, instrumental situations, he was very developed in that way, conducting.
A project like this, did you have an idea and then took it to Orrin, or did Orrin bring an idea to you? How was that? I imagine it was a very fluid relationship?

Yeah we had a good relationship and we sort of let one project be a gauge in which to do something else. I think I did some things with strings and some things with vocals was a good departure, but related in some ways. I guess I had my way of not necessarily letting one particular situation dominate the other. If I used horns then I would maybe add voices to it and I liked that, or strings, whatever. I try to come up with different combinations to make it good for me too, give me . . .
You and Bill worked well together.
Yeah, Bill Fischer and I worked very well . . .
He knew voices, and Orrin, all three. Yeah because he (Bill) was close to Orrin too.
